column3: Wood in general: the species-independent equilibrium moisture content of the Wood Handbook (no species named)
column4: Hailwood-Horrobin form fitted by Simpson (1973) to the EMC data of the 1955 Wood Handbook; Table 4-2 (temperature -1.1 to 132.2 C, relative humidity 5 to 95 percent) is calculated from it
column5: EMC(%) = (1800/W) [K h/(1 - K h) + (K1 K h + 2 K1 K2 K^2 h^2)/(1 + K1 K h + K1 K2 K^2 h^2)], h the relative humidity as a decimal, with W = 349 + 1.29 T + 0.0135 T^2, K = 0.805 + 0.000736 T - 0.00000273 T^2, K1 = 6.27 - 0.00938 T - 0.000303 T^2, K2 = 1.91 + 0.0407 T - 0.000293 T^2 for T in degrees Celsius, as printed (Equation 4-5). The polynomial argument is the Celsius temperature, so the linear and quadratic coefficients carry K-1 and K-2 (a Celsius degree equals a kelvin) and an evaluator must subtract 273.15 K first. Validity is the span of Table 4-2, which the chapter says was calculated from this equation; outside it the fit is not documented. The form is a sorption (desorption-averaged) EMC, not a hysteresis model
